eIF3d/eIF3e Knockdown TE Changes (With/Without Spike-in) vs Literature

Kate

2026-07-21

Purpose

All “ours” si3d/si3e TE numbers in this notebook (both with-spike and no-spike legs, in every table and plot) are 1+4hr time-regressed normoxia results — i.e. deFunction_time_normalized() fit on the 1hr+4hr normoxia samples jointly with hours as a batch covariate, not a single-timepoint result. This is noted here, in the notebook text, rather than in the plots themselves — the plot labels/titles below say “normoxia” only, without “1+4hr”, to keep them concise.

Fourth notebook in the spike-in vs literature comparison subsection. Extends 03_bar_te_si3d_si3e_vs_literature.Rmd’s final combined eIF3d/eIF3e plots to add a no-spike-in bar right after each with-spike-in bar for our own si3d/si3e data (matching the with/without spike-in comparison style used in notebooks 01/02, now applied to the knockdown-vs-sictrl TE comparison instead of the hypoxia-vs-normoxia one).

No saved no-spike-in si3d/si3e TE (1+4hr) file exists anywhere in the repo. Checked: analyzing_spikeins.Rmd computes per-timepoint (1/4/24hr) si3d/si3e no-spike TE in memory only (si3d_nospike_results, si3e_nospike_results — no write_csv). si3e_si3d_normoxia_1and4hr_timecourse.Rmd computes the exact 1+4hr time-regressed no-spike TE we need (res_te_si3d_nospike_1and4hr, res_te_si3e_nospike_1and4hr) for its density-plot comparison, but also never saves it to a file. So unlike every other “with-spike” number in this subsection, this leg is computed fresh here — following that notebook’s exact method — and saved, so it becomes reusable going forward.

  • Method, copied exactly from si3e_si3d_normoxia_1and4hr_timecourse.Rmd: deFunction_time_normalized(control_condition = "si3d"/"si3e", test_condition = "sictrl", mode = "TE"), with spikeInMatrix = NULL, keepSpikes = NULL and a createNormMatrix(..., spikein = NULL) normalization matrix for the no-spike leg. Same control_condition/test_condition assignment as the saved with-spike files used in notebook 03 — log2(sictrl/si3d) or log2(sictrl/si3e) — so no sign flip is needed between the with-spike and no-spike legs; both already share our positive-means-promoted convention.

run_nospike_te <- function(treatment_val) {
  metadata_tp <- metadata %>%
    filter(condition == "normoxia") %>%
    filter(treatment %in% c("sictrl", treatment_val)) %>%
    filter(hours %in% c(1, 4)) %>%
    mutate(comparison_variable = treatment)
  metadata_tp$hours <- as.factor(metadata_tp$hours)

  counts_tp <- allCounts[, metadata_tp$sample_name]

  normMatrix_nospike <- createNormMatrix(
    allCounts = counts_tp,
    metadata = metadata_tp,
    control_condition = treatment_val,
    spikein = NULL,
    keepSpikes = NULL
  )

  deFunction_time_normalized(
    countsMatrix = counts_tp,
    allCounts_Norm = normMatrix_nospike,
    metadata = metadata_tp,
    control_condition = treatment_val,
    test_condition = "sictrl",
    spikeInMatrix = NULL,
    keepSpikes = NULL,
    mode = "TE"
  )
}

Computational checks

te_data <- bind_rows(with_spike_data, no_spike_data)

stopifnot(
  "log2FoldChange must be finite" =
    all(is.finite(te_data$log2FoldChange[!is.na(te_data$log2FoldChange)])),
  "padj must be within [0, 1]" =
    all(te_data$padj >= 0 & te_data$padj <= 1, na.rm = TRUE)
)
cat("log2FoldChange/padj range checks passed\n")
## log2FoldChange/padj range checks passed

Count significant genes (|log2FC| >= 0.5, padj < 0.05)

lfc_cutoff <- 0.5
padj_cutoff <- 0.05

sig_counts_si3d_si3e_spike <- te_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj), padj < padj_cutoff, abs(log2FoldChange) >= lfc_cutoff) %>%
  mutate(Direction = if_else(log2FoldChange > 0, "Up", "Down")) %>%
  dplyr::count(treatment, spike_status, Direction, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(
    Direction = factor(Direction, levels = c("Up", "Down")),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("si3d", "si3e")),
    spike_status = factor(spike_status, levels = c("With spike-in", "No spike-in"))
  )

print(sig_counts_si3d_si3e_spike)

Combined plots: with/without spike-in ours vs all literature comparisons

Same design as notebook 03’s final plots: bar color = source (Okabe-Ito), label color = Up (vermillion) / Down (blue). Our si3d/si3e now contribute two rows each (with spike-in, then no spike-in immediately after), sharing the same hue since both represent “ours” for that target — only the axis label distinguishes spike status.

  mutate(
    target = recode(as.character(treatment), si3d = "eIF3d", si3e = "eIF3e"),

make_target_plot <- function(df, target_label) {
  df <- droplevels(df)
  source_levels_local <- intersect(all_source_levels, levels(df$source))
  n_ours_local <- sum(grepl("^\\*\\*", source_levels_local))
  dodge_local <- position_dodge(width = 0.7)
  y_pad_local <- 0.20 * max(df$n)

  ggplot(df, aes(x = source, y = n, fill = source, group = Direction)) +
    geom_col(position = dodge_local, width = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n, color = Direction), position = dodge_local,
              vjust = -0.4, size = 8, fontface = "bold", key_glyph = "point") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = n_ours_local + 0.5, linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.7, color = "grey30") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = source_colors, guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Up = up_dark, Down = down_dark), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(df$n) + y_pad_local)) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = source_levels_local) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 7))) +
    labs(title = paste0(target_label, " TE changes: ours (with/without spike-in, normoxia)\nvs all literature comparisons"),
         subtitle = "Cutoffs shown per bar group. Each literature source uses its own reported totals and cutoffs (see notebook 03).\nOurs = Okabe-Ito; literature = grey. Label color = Up (vermillion) / Down (blue).",
         x = NULL, y = "# sig genes") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 24) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          legend.text = element_text(size = 21),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 25),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 15),
          axis.line.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = 22),
          axis.line.x = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_markdown(size = 18, angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
}
